user_questions.question: Before I propose changes, three decisions: (1) How should an account be flagged? (a) new formula checkbox 'SLA Expiring Soon' on Account (recommended: always current, no automation); (b) scheduled flow sets Contract_Status__c = 'Pending Renewal' (value exists; 2 accounts already use it); (c) scheduled flow sets a stored checkbox. (2) How should account managers act on it? (a) an Account list view of flagged accounts; (b) email or task to the owner; (c) both. (3) SLAExpirationDate__c is empty on all 200 accounts and nothing populates it except manual entry on the Account layouts. (a) proceed and document manual entry as the data dependency (recommended); (b) include a bulk-load procedure in the spec.
user_questions.simulated_answer: (1) Formula checkbox 'SLA Expiring Soon'. (2) A list view; no emails. (3) No preference; use your recommended default.

skill_friction: A new field needs FLS to be usable, but SKILL.md and spec-format only say broad or integration grants are open decisions; there is no guidance on whether a new dedicated permission set is the least-access default or 'behavior nobody asked for'. I chose a new PermissionSet and dropped AskCoworker's Agentforce_Reference_App grant.

Permission set assignment is a data step (PermissionSetAssignment). The content rule says every data operation needs backup and rollback steps, which fits a bulk load but reads oddly for an assignment; no guidance on this.

AskCoworker labels facts I sent in the message as '[Verified: prior session]'. The response-handling table treats 'prior session' facts as needing verification, so it is unclear whether echoed established facts must be re-checked or can be accepted as-is.
Some list view settings (sort order) are not part of ListView metadata; spec-format has no guidance on UI-only settings, so I recorded them as an assumption in Section 8.

DataStreamDefinition is not queryable with the allowed commands, so AskCoworker's 'no Account data stream' claim cannot be verified; Section 5 guidance is just 'Not applicable' vs 'not specified', with no place for 'not applicable, but a reported unverifiable claim'.

Step 5 lists 'depends on data nothing provides' as a scope-check trigger, but when the data can be entered by hand on existing layouts it is unclear whether that counts as 'provided'; the simulated intent did not cover it and the answer was 'no preference'.
